findings.title: `metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError for integrations that have no `sender`
findings.body: The check indexes `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` directly. Only integrations created by the `installation` webhook have `sender` in their metadata. An Integration row built by this pipeline's `build_integration` (access_token, icon, domain_name, account_type, ...) has no `sender` key. If such an Integration still exists after its OrganizationIntegrations are removed, for example when an org uninstalls and then reinstalls, this line raises KeyError and the user gets a 500 instead of the install or the error page. I could not see every path that writes this metadata. Fix: use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and return `error(...)` when it is missing or does not match.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found now only tests a state mismatch, not the 404 path
findings.body: Before, this test checked that a GitHub 404 for the installation showed "The GitHub installation could not be found.". Now it sends a `state` (`ddd023...`) that does not match the pipeline signature and asserts the generic "Invalid installation request.". The request fails at the state check in OAuthLoginView and never reaches `build_integration`, so the 404 stub is never used and nothing tests the installation-not-found handling anymore. Fix: send the correct state and code, then assert the original not-found message.
